title: Strong monoidal transport of balancing and quotient-action diagrams
statement:
Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be monoidal categories and $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ a strong monoidal functor with tensorator $t_{U,V}:FU\otimes FV\xrightarrow{\sim}F(U\otimes V)$ [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor]. Let $R,S$ be monoid objects, $\varphi:R\to S$ a monoid morphism [sk-def-sfb-ring-object], and $M$ a left $R$-module with action $\gamma_M$ [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Write $m_S$ for multiplication on $S$ and $\alpha^{\mathcal C},\alpha^{\mathcal D}$ for the associators. Set
\[
a_M=(m_S\circ(1_S\otimes\varphi))\otimes1_M,\quad b_M=(1_S\otimes\gamma_M)\circ\alpha^{\mathcal C}_{S,R,M}:
(S\otimes R)\otimes M\rightrightarrows S\otimes M.
\]
Equip $FR,FS,FM$ with the transported monoid and module structures [def-sfb-modobj-transport], so $m_{FS}=F(m_S)\circ t_{S,S}$ and $\gamma_{FM}=F(\gamma_M)\circ t_{R,M}$. Define $a'_M,b'_M$ by the same displayed formulas in $\mathcal D$, using $F\varphi$, $m_{FS}$, $\gamma_{FM}$ and $\alpha^{\mathcal D}$. Then the isomorphisms
\[
t_{0,M}=t_{S,M},\qquad t_{1,M}=t_{S\otimes R,M}\circ(t_{S,R}\otimes1_{FM})
\]
satisfy $F(a_M)\circ t_{1,M}=t_{0,M}\circ a'_M$ and $F(b_M)\circ t_{1,M}=t_{0,M}\circ b'_M$.
Moreover, let $P$ be any $S$-module with action $\delta_P$, and let $q:S\otimes M\to P$ satisfy
\[
\delta_P\circ(1_S\otimes q)=q\circ(m_S\otimes1_M)\circ(\alpha^{\mathcal C}_{S,S,M})^{-1}.
\]
For the transported action $\delta_{FP}=F(\delta_P)\circ t_{S,P}$, the morphism $\widehat q=F(q)\circ t_{0,M}$ satisfies
\[
\delta_{FP}\circ(1_{FS}\otimes\widehat q)=\widehat q\circ(m_{FS}\otimes1_{FM})\circ(\alpha^{\mathcal D}_{FS,FS,FM})^{-1}.
\]
No preservation of colimits by $F$, commutativity of $R,S$, or choice of a quotient object is assumed.

proof.text: Use the naturality and associativity equations stated in [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor], with $t$ in place of $\mu$. Tensor bifunctoriality [def-sfb-monoidal-category] gives $(t_{S,R}^{-1}\otimes1_{FM})\circ(t_{S,R}\otimes1_{FM})=1$ and the reverse identity. Hence $t_{1,M}$ is an isomorphism with inverse $(t_{S,R}^{-1}\otimes1_{FM})\circ t_{S\otimes R,M}^{-1}$; $t_{0,M}$ is already a specified tensorator isomorphism.

proof.text:
Put $k=m_S\circ(1_S\otimes\varphi)$ and $k'=m_{FS}\circ(1_{FS}\otimes F\varphi)$. The transported multiplication is that of [def-sfb-modobj-transport]. Naturality in [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor], for $(1_S,\varphi)$, gives
\[
k'=F(m_S)\circ t_{S,S}\circ(1_{FS}\otimes F\varphi)
=F(k)\circ t_{S,R}.
\]
Naturality again, now for $(k,1_M)$, therefore gives
\[
F(a_M)\circ t_{1,M}
=t_{S,M}\circ(F(k)\otimes1_{FM})\circ(t_{S,R}\otimes1_{FM})
=t_{0,M}\circ(k'\otimes1_{FM})=t_{0,M}\circ a'_M.
\]

source.place: Tag 0FFL, definition-functor-monoidal-categories: tensorator naturality and associativity diagram, with the inverse associator convention of Tag 0FFK

proof.text:
The associativity axiom of [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor] at $(S,R,M)$ reads
\[
F(\alpha^{\mathcal C}_{S,R,M})\circ t_{1,M}
=t_{S,R\otimes M}\circ(1_{FS}\otimes t_{R,M})\circ\alpha^{\mathcal D}_{FS,FR,FM}.
\]
Postcompose with $F(1_S\otimes\gamma_M)$ and apply tensorator naturality for $(1_S,\gamma_M)$. Using the transported action from [def-sfb-modobj-transport] gives
\[
F(b_M)\circ t_{1,M}
=t_{S,M}\circ(1_{FS}\otimes(F(\gamma_M)\circ t_{R,M}))\circ\alpha^{\mathcal D}_{FS,FR,FM}
=t_{0,M}\circ b'_M.
\]

proof.text:
For the last assertion abbreviate $\alpha_C=\alpha^{\mathcal C}_{S,S,M}$ and $\alpha_D=\alpha^{\mathcal D}_{FS,FS,FM}$, and set
\[
u=t_{S,S\otimes M}\circ(1_{FS}\otimes t_{S,M}),\qquad
v=t_{S\otimes S,M}\circ(t_{S,S}\otimes1_{FM}).
\]
Associativity in [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor] gives $F(\alpha_C)\circ v=u\circ\alpha_D$. Precomposing with $\alpha_D^{-1}$ and postcomposing with $F(\alpha_C^{-1})$ yields
\[
v\circ\alpha_D^{-1}=F(\alpha_C^{-1})\circ u.
\]
The cancellation uses only $F(\alpha_C^{-1})\circ F(\alpha_C)=F(1)=1$.

source.place: Tag 0FFL, definition-functor-monoidal-categories: tensorator naturality and associativity diagram, with the inverse associator convention of Tag 0FFK

proof.text:
By the transported action formula [def-sfb-modobj-transport], tensor bifunctoriality [def-sfb-monoidal-category], and naturality [def-sfb-strong-monoidal-functor] for $(1_S,q)$, the left side of the required equation is
\[
F(\delta_P)\circ t_{S,P}\circ(1_{FS}\otimes F(q))\circ(1_{FS}\otimes t_{S,M})
=F(\delta_P\circ(1_S\otimes q))\circ u.
\]
For its right side, substitute $m_{FS}=F(m_S)\circ t_{S,S}$ and use naturality for $(m_S,1_M)$ and step 4:
\[
\begin{aligned}
\widehat q\circ(m_{FS}\otimes1_{FM})\circ\alpha_D^{-1}
&=F(q)\circ t_{S,M}\circ(F(m_S)\otimes1_{FM})\circ(t_{S,S}\otimes1_{FM})\circ\alpha_D^{-1}\\
&=F(q\circ(m_S\otimes1_M))\circ v\circ\alpha_D^{-1}\\
&=F(q\circ(m_S\otimes1_M)\circ\alpha_C^{-1})\circ u.
\end{aligned}
\]
The assumed equation for $q$ makes these expressions equal. All displayed equalities are substitutions, functoriality, or the explicitly cited coherence equations.
